notes: SINGLE RUN per configuration — every stddev in this report is 0 and means nothing. Treat the pass rates as one sample, not a distribution.
The delta is carried almost entirely by eval-0 (build mode): 100% vs 62%. eval-1 was 100% vs 80%, and eval-2 was a dead tie at 100% vs 100%.

NON-DISCRIMINATING: 'no fabricated quotations' and 'no samurai cosplay' passed 6/6. They measure nothing today. Keep them as regression guards — they would catch a future regression — but they inflate every score and should be read as floor, not signal.

SATURATED EVAL: eval-2 (study mode) scored 8/8 for both configurations. The baseline correctly explained the Fire book, all three sen, and placed iwao no mi as its closing teaching — unprompted, and it quoted the Harris rendering accurately while flagging the Hosokawa anecdote as possibly apocryphal. Either the skill adds nothing in pure study mode or the assertions are too easy. This eval needs harder assertions before it can inform anything.

VACUOUS PASSES: in eval-0 the baseline passed 'uses at most three named Fire-book tactics' and 'every named tactic is cashed out' by using ZERO tactics. Those two passes are worth ~15 points of its 62% and are meaningless. Rewrite as 'uses between one and three' to make them discriminate.

The baseline outputs are strong on substance and weak on structure. eval-0's baseline invented a 'Constraint Loop' (five numbers, five-rung ladder, four gates) that is genuinely good operational advice — arguably more specific on junk-removal economics than the with-skill run. What it did not produce was a method the user could return to by name, which is precisely what the prompt asked for. The skill's value here is durable structure, not better business analysis.

COST: with_skill averaged 64,033 tokens vs 39,288 (+63%) and 213.6s vs 192.8s (+11%). The overhead is reference-file reading. On eval-2, where the delta was zero, that cost bought nothing — worth checking whether study-mode questions can be served by one reference file instead of several.

Assertions 1, 5 and 11 in eval-0 (five rings present, initiative declared, Dokkodo written) are structurally skill-shaped: a no-skill run can essentially never pass them. They are fair as a test of whether the skill delivers its promised artifact, but they are not evidence that the artifact is better — the human review is what settles that.
